title: Thee, Jesus, Full of Truth and Grace
description: Thee, Jesus, Full of Truth and Grace in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 329.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thee, Je-sus, full of truth and grace, Thee, Sa-viour, we a-dore, Thee in af-flic-tion's fur-nace praise, And mag-ni-fy thy power.

lines: Thee, Jesus, full of truth and grace,
Thy power, in human weakness shown,
We now thy guardian presence own,
Thee, Son of man, by faith we see,
The fire our graces shall refine,

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
